Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
212 PM EDT Mon Aug 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 208 PM EDT Monday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast at this time.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 208 PM EDT Monday...

1. Showers and thunderstorms expected this afternoon and 
evening.

2. Drier weather Tuesday and Wednesday with another round of 
showers and thunderstorms on Thursday.

3. Showers possible on Friday with drier weather expected 
Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 208 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A warm front lifting north across New York this morning 
will be the catalyst for showers and thunderstorm development as we 
head into the mid afternoon hours and well into the evening. The 
latest high-resolution guidance has slowed the onset of 
precipitation into our forecast area until around 5 PM across far 
western portions of northern New York with rain and thunderstorms 
not entering Vermont until after 8 PM. The best instability doesn't 
develop until after 00Z as mid-leve lapse rates begin to steepen. 
Anywhere from 1000 to 1500 J/kg of MLCAPE is forecasted to develop 
which will be coupled with 40 knots of 0-6km shear. This should help 
produce some strong to localized severe thunderstorms and SPC has 
placed a marginal risk for severe weather across northern New York 
and the northern half of Vermont due to the increasing instability. 
The lack of surface convergence should keep the areal coverage low 
but it wouldn't be surprising to see some stronger storms following 
sunset tonight. In addition, we could see some impressive 
instantaneous rainfall rates with PWATS above the 80th percentile so 
we can't rule out some ponding of water on roads to localized 
flooding. These storms will be moving quickly (40 knots of 0-6 
shear) which will mitigate the flood threat but will also help to 
move these storms east of the Connecticut river shortly after 
midnight.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Outside of a start shower across the Adirondacks or 
Green Mountains, quiet and dry weather is expected on both Tuesday 
and Wednesday. Weak surface high pressure will try to build north 
but will generally be suppressed due to low pressure to our north and 
east. Nevertheless, we should see some clearing in the skies midweek 
with Wednesday showing partly to mostly sunny skies for the partial 
eclipse. Temperatures will be in the mid 70s to lower 80s with winds 
generally from the west/northwest at 10 mph or less. Patchy dense 
fog will be possible in the favorable river valleys Wednesday 
morning given the upcoming rainfall this afternoon, light winds, and 
clearing skies.

The next system will move through the region on Thursday as a strong 
cold front approaches the region. The frontal timing has slowed 
slightly in the last 24 hours with the frontal passage now expected 
to be closer to peak heating. This has caused both the AI and 
machine learning algorithms to slightly increase the severe 
potential for Thursday. We will once again be working with 1000 to 
1500 J/kg of ML CAPE and 40 knots of 0-6 km shear which is more than 
sufficient to see organized convection capable of producing strong 
to locally severe storms.

KEY MESSAGE 3: The upper level low will close off to our east Friday 
morning which will help bring some recycled maritime into our region 
under an easterly flow regime. This will likely spark additional 
rain showers across the northern and western slopes of the Green 
Mountains with upslope conditions. However, it seems likely that 
most valley locations will generally be on the drier side on Friday. 
Deep layer ridging will build across the region late Friday through 
the weekend with dry, seasonably cool, and less humid air expected. 
Highs should top out in the mid to upper 70s with dewpoints dropping 
into the 40s each afternoon and plentiful sunshine.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 18Z Tuesday...A warm front and weak cold front will bring
increasing chances of showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and
evening with drier conditions late Tuesday. A few of these showers
and storms could produce localized heavy rainfall, but flow will be
progressive enough to keep the cells moving. About 30% chance of
some showers spreading from west to east across northern New York
and Vermont through 00Z Tuesday, becoming more widespread into the
evening. Highest chance overall of precipitation will be from 22Z
Monday through 04Z Tuesday, which could lower visibilities 3-5 
miles, briefly lower in any heavier downpours. There is also the
potential for thunderstorms during this period, most likely at 
BTV, SLK, MPV, and MSS. With and following these showers and 
storms early Tuesday morning, low level moisture is expected to 
linger at several sites, and any breaks in clouds could lead to 
quick radiational fog. Most likely site for IFR conditions is 
SLK from 06Z-13Z Tuesday, though MPV and EFK both have some 
potential for cig and vis degradations around this time as well.
Much will depend on the strength of the inversion that develops
in the subsidence behind the storms, and the spots that see 
more rainfall from the afternoon/evening storms will be more 
likely to have fog, especially those that have clearing skies 
and lighter winds. Winds this afternoon and into tonight will be
mainly southwesterly, turning more west-northwesterly Tuesday 
morning, following the passage of the cold front. Some brief 
LLWS is possible Tuesday morning as winds aloft turn and 
increase more quickly than winds at the surface.

Outlook...

Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: VFR. Likely SHRA, Chance TSRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
Channeled southerly winds in the 15 to 20 knot range will
continue across much of Lake Champlain through 10 PM. A frontal
passage late this afternoon will yield a quick increase in winds
across the lake with gusts upwards to 30 knots between 7 PM and
10 PM. Waves will generally be in the 1-2 ft range this
afternoon with an increase to 2-3 feet this evening. Winds and
waves will quickly subside after midnight.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
